title: Monetary Policy Report—July 2024
summary: The Bank of Canada released its July 2024 Monetary Policy Report showing that CPI inflation is moving toward the 2% target, core inflation has eased significantly, and upside price pressures are no longer broad-based. The Bank simultaneously reduced its overnight policy rate by 25 basis points to 4.5%. Core inflation is projected to ease to approximately 2.5% in the second half of 2024, with full return to target expected later in 2025.
key_points: Bank of Canada cut overnight policy rate by 25 bps to 4.5% (Bank Rate 4.75%, deposit rate 4.5%)
CPI inflation is moving closer to the 2% target; price pressures are no longer broad-based
Core inflation projected to ease to ~2.5% in H2 2024, returning sustainably to 2% later in 2025
Canadian economic growth has picked up but remains weak relative to population growth
Global economy expected to grow at ~3% over the projection horizon; US growth has slowed
Bank judges risks to inflation outlook to be balanced between upside and downside
Wage growth remains elevated; services inflation proving persistent
why_it_matters: This quarterly report provides the Bank of Canada's comprehensive assessment of the Canadian economy and inflation outlook, informing market expectations for future rate decisions. The 25 bps rate cut marks a policy pivot, signaling the Bank's growing confidence that inflation is being brought under control. Markets closely track the balance of risks and the timeline for returning to the 2% target.
macro_context: The Bank of Canada pivoted to easing with a 25 bps rate cut, reflecting progress on inflation. Excess supply in the economy (driven by strong population growth adding to labor supply) is expected to continue pulling inflation down. However, services inflation remains persistent due to elevated wage growth, and shelter inflation is being kept high by rent and mortgage interest costs. The Bank projects CPI will temporarily fall below core inflation (due to gasoline prices) before rising modestly in H1 2025 and then sustainably returning to 2%.
